extracted.intended_audience: artificial intelligence researchers, cognitive scientists, and students interested in problem-solving heuristics
extracted.subtask_description: Characterize George Polya's corpus of heuristics for human problem solving and evaluate their relation and applicability to AI, including the roles of auxiliary problems, learning, and problem-space representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify 'What is the unknown? The data? The condition?' and examine sufficiency/contradiction; draw a figure; separate parts of the condition; write them down; introduce suitable notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions and directives from Polya's main method: check if the condition is satisfiable/sufficient/insufficient/redundant/contradictory; diagramming and explicit decomposition are central. Example: in geometry problems, drawing a figure often makes relations explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devise a plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate an approach: ask whether you've seen the problem before, know a related problem or theorem, or can restate/transform the problem; consider auxiliary elements and related simpler or general problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's checklist: 'Seen the problem before? Know a related problem? Given a related solved problem, use its result? its method? Could an auxiliary element help?' Strategies include restating, going back to definitions, solving related problems (special, general, analogous), solving parts, and keeping portions of the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry out the plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute the devised plan and pursue the intermediate goals/subplans required to reach the overall solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya treats the plan as a symbolic object that must be discovered, criticized and revised; carrying out the plan may require applying submethods and verifying intermediate steps. Some methods (e.g., proving-as-you-go) bypass separate verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the result and argument, and reflect on the solution to learn from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's final step includes checking correctness, seeking alternate derivations, and using the solution to generate methods/results for future problems. The 'Look back' stage is explicitly for learning and preparing for future problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the result/argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify correctness of the derived result and the soundness of the reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verification tactics appropriate to the domain (e.g., algebraic checks, dimensional analysis, re-derivation). Polya emphasizes explicit checking as part of 'Examine the solution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive the same result differently
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain the result by an alternative method or interpretation to strengthen understanding and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya recommends re-deriving results (Interpret the formula) to gain insight and produce methods useful for future problems; alternative derivations can reveal deeper structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the result to obtain new problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform solved problems into new ones (e.g., switch unknowns) to build reusable problem/method stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya encourages 'switch the unknown' and creating derived problems so each solved problem contributes to future solving capability; pedagogically this trains 'education of the will' and accumulation of problem repertoire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct and manage attention to relevant aspects of the problem; attending to the 'right things' is necessary for problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya emphasizes coaching learners to attend to salient features; attention cueing leads to memory retrieval ('memory must be tickled') and is more than mere input assembly—it helps activate relevant knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tickle memory / mobilize prior knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Evoking related prior problems, theorems, or experiences by attending to cues so that previously acquired knowledge becomes available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's questions aim at mobilizing formerly acquired knowledge ('Have you seen it before?'). The process is often indirect—attending to X suggests Y. This is consistent with encoding-specific retrieval and production-system models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem solver motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the problem solver has desire and concentration to pursue solutions; motivation affects perseverance and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya argues that 'the intelligent problem-solver... must desire earnestly to obtain its solution' and that teaching problem solving involves educating the will. Social/contextual factors (awaken curiosity) are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgoals and subplans
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize problem solving around intermediate goals (subgoals) and submethods; plans themselves are methods and symbolic objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's main method and many of his techniques rely on forming subgoals (e.g., intermediate constructs) and treating the plan as a manipulable object to be found and evaluated; this connects to means-ends analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods should be observable and empirically detectable
rubrics_metrics.description: A method (e.g., understand-devise-carry out-look back) has observable stages that can be empirically identified in problem-solving behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newell & Simon-style protocol analyses can detect whether the plan exists prior to implementation; observable markers support empirical study and mechanization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reductio ad absurdum
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the negation of the claim, derive a contradiction, conclude the original is true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A classical proof method; Polya lists it as a named method with explicit three-step structure. Useful in mathematical reasoning and formal proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of loci (construction via loci)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce a geometric construction to constructing one point, split conditions into two parts each yielding loci (lines/circles), then intersect loci to locate the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya presents this classical compass-and-straightedge construction heuristic as a systematic procedure; useful in geometric construction problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go back to definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand the working representation by explicitly using definitions of terms to reveal new relations and paths to solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although often appearing as a slogan, this is a symbolic procedure that can produce workable transformations and new subproblems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of convertible transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply lossless transformations iteratively to create a chain of equivalent expressions/problems so a solution to a transformed problem maps back to the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method constrains transformations to those that preserve information; typical of algebraic manipulations and many symbolic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working backwards / form inverse problem space
rubrics_metrics.description: Invert operators to form the inverse problem space where the desired state becomes the initial state; solve in the inverse space and map solution back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya frames backward-working as constructing an inverse space with inverted operators. It's powerful but not always possible; it corresponds to forming inverse problems explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accumulate knowledge (examine parts and retry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine a part of the problem to gain new knowledge, then retry the whole problem using the expanded description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method recommends iterative enrichment of the problem representation (adding derived relations) and then reattempting the main goal; analogous to certain AI transform-then-retry strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test by dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Check formulas/results by verifying dimensional consistency of quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapted from dimensional analysis: ensure units match (A = 3 implies units equal); a domain-specific verification trick particularly useful in physics/engineering contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret the formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Map algebraic/formulaic results back into the problem's model/diagram to derive alternative constructions or explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreting subexpressions as model components suggests new derivations; useful for generating constructive proofs or geometric interpretations from algebraic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switch the unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a new problem by swapping the roles of an unknown and a given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya encourages using solved problems as a source of new problems by interchanging unknowns and givens; can produce fresh perspectives and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use auxiliary problems (results, methods, suggestions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate auxiliary problems (special cases, analogues, or simpler problems) and use them for their results, their methods, or to suggest further approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya heavily emphasizes auxiliary problems: ~50% of basic heuristic questions and ~60% of How to Solve It examples involve auxiliaries. Examples: using triangle CG to solve tetrahedron CG (use method), special-case ships problem (use result).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of auxiliary problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and exploit a wide diversity of auxiliary problems (varied sources and types) to increase chances of relevance and transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya argues diversity increases coverage of the problem-space 'perimeter' and reduces overlap; pedagogically, diverse problem repertoire maximizes long-run problem-solving power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for future problem solving (learning orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat each problem as preparation for future problems—extract methods, results, and insights to expand capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's 'Look back' explicitly instructs learners to convert solved problems into reusable rules; Newell frames this as expanding the interior of a problem-space capability and thickening the rind of solvable problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility assessment of inductions and analogies
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the plausibility or credibility of inductive inferences and analogical transfers rather than treating them as automatically reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's Mathematics and Plausible Reasoning seeks a calculus of credibility: criteria and heuristics for when analogies/inductions are reliable. AI must consider criteria for analogical strength and defeasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-space representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent problems as states and operators in a problem space; methods correspond to traversals and transformations within these spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's methods can be re-cast in AI problem-space terms (e.g., working backwards as inverse operators); representation choice critically affects which methods are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object-centered problem spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate problem spaces centered on objects (e.g., geometric figures, diagrams) with operators acting on these object-based representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya often works with concrete object representations (figures, diagrams); object-centered spaces make many auxiliary or connection methods natural (e.g., geometric constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tame vs wild subproblems
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish 'tame' (methodically-generated, pre-defined relation to main problem) from 'wild' (auxiliary, weakly-related, unpredictable) subproblems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newell argues AI handles tame/domesticated subproblems well but struggles with wild auxiliary problems whose relation to the main problem is not predefined; wild subproblems require different search/connection abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection subproblems
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate and solve the subproblem that makes an auxiliary problem relevant to the main problem (e.g., constructing the bridge between auxiliary result and main problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's use of auxiliaries requires solving 'connection problems'—often a separate well-defined task (constructing an augmented diagram, applying a velocity transform). Success depends on the ability to represent and construct the connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce to special cases / use special-case auxiliaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify the main problem by reducing to special cases (auxiliaries) that are easier to solve, then map results back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: two-ships problem reduced to case with one ship at rest; trapezoid-construction uses introducing auxiliary result into original figure. Reduction requires a viable mapping/connection step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce auxiliary element (augment the problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment the given problem (e.g., add a line, add a constructed object) to create a problem whose solution helps the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya suggests adding elements to figures or restating to create an augmented problem; the augmented problem often lives in the same problem space and may simplify solution if the connection is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct explicit problem spaces from givens
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive the problem space (states and operators) required for auxiliary or connection subproblems from the givens and the intended functional orientation (e.g., reduce main problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya and Newell identify that building the right problem space (e.g., adding velocity operators for two-ships) is a key early step; AI must be able to construct such spaces from domain information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observable plan formation prior to implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure plans are formed before execution—plans exist as symbolic objects and can be detected experimentally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's methodology treats plans as explicit entities; programmatically, manufacture of plans allows critique and revision before execution, and supports empirical protocol analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize diversity/perimeter of solvable problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and learn problems/methods that maximize the 'perimeter' (boundary) of solvable problem space rather than redundant overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya/Newell model: the solver's capability is the interior plus a rind of new problems reachable by methods; choosing diverse problems expands coverage more than similar ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical tractability test for wild subproblems
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating applicability to AI, test whether wild auxiliary/connection subproblems are tractable by attempting implementations rather than assuming impossibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newell conjectures many wild-subproblem tasks may be tractable when AI attempts them; cites historical advances (DENDRAL, MYCIN) where AI extended into new domains successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use methods as symbolic procedures amenable to mechanization
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which of Polya's methods are straightforward symbolic procedures (suitable for programs) vs. those that are informal and require richer architectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'go back to definitions' and 'sequence of convertible transformations' are straightforward for symbolic systems; 'attention' and 'motivation' require different architectural supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess relationship between heuristics and problem content
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether problem-solving success depends more on general heuristics or on content-specific knowledge of problems themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One thesis Newell examines: perhaps crucial knowledge lies in the content of particular problems (not in transferable heuristics), which affects how AI should prioritize encoding domain knowledge vs. general heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate analogical/inductive transfer strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge when analogy or induction yields reliable transfer; consider similarity, structural alignment, and justificatory evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya's focus on plausible reasoning seeks criteria for when analogical inference is credible; AI needs formal metrics or heuristics for analogical mapping and assessing transfer risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe methods in examples and dialogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn heuristics by worked examples and hypothetical dialogues that reveal stepwise attention-directing and teacher-student interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya heavily uses micro-essays and dialogues to communicate heuristics; pedagogically, worked examples and explicated reasoning paths are key to transferring heuristic knowledge.
